text:
maya: quick heads up — I noticed a weird divergence between route-level quotas and the telemetry sampling we get for cross-route traffic. Some users hit quota blocks on route A but console metrics show requests served on route B.
sameer: hmm that's concerning. do you have an example trace id?
maya: yeh, trace 0b3f9c. payloads show header x-route=route-a but the routed backend was route-b per the logs.
lee: could be config propagation lag after the recent config apply? ops-bot showed a batch apply earlier.
ops-bot: DeployBot: applied config set "route-quota-update" by @maya at 6172109800 to clusters [us-east-1, eu-west-1].
maya: I double-checked — the console preview showed the new routing policy but the dry-run flag was ON for quota enforcement. maybe dry-run vs apply got out of sync across services.
ali: can you paste the snippet of the routing+quota config? curious about scoped defaults vs explicit route overrides.
maya: sure:
```
{
  "routes": {
    "route-a": { "quota": 1000, "sample_rate": 0.05 },
    "route-b": { "quota": 5000 }
  },
  "defaults": { "quota": 2000, "sample_rate": 0.1 }
}
```
maya: note route-b inherits defaults for sample_rate, but route-a is explicit. logs show route-a requests sampled at 0.1 which matches defaults, not 0.05.
lee: that suggests the sampler component read the old defaults (0.1) while the router used the new per-route quota. means our config snapshotting between services isn't atomic.
sameer: agreed. we version configs with a commit id, right? should the router and telemetry use the same commit id header during request lifetime?
katie: we tried to avoid per-request headers to reduce overhead. instead we push a global active_config pointer. but that pointer update can be applied at different times in different clusters.
ali: possible fixes: 1) make config publish atomic via two-phase commit (slow), 2) have services check config commit id on startup and refuse partial states, 3) include commit id in request metadata for accurate telemetry attribution.
maya: option 3 seems lightweight and gives telemetry exactness. downside is we need to plumb commit id through internal calls.
lee: another angle: for console visibility, show the active commit id and apply window. add a per-route rollout status in the UI (applied/pending/failed). that helps Ops surface partial rollouts.
sameer: telemetry sampling correctness is important for our regression alerts — wrong sample_rate skews anomaly detection.
katie: engineering effort estimate: commit-id header plumbing is small in router proxy (~2 days) + telemetry read change (~1 day) + console UI (~1 day). two-phase commit would be weeks.
ali: also add a check in the config apply job that validates clusters have consistent active pointers within a window, and emit warning if drift > 30s.
maya: I'm happy to own the commit-id header PR for router proxy. can someone pick up the telemetry side?
sameer: I can take telemetry. will add compatibility so missing commit id falls back to best-effort attribution and emit a metric.
katie: I'll add a console card showing active commit id + last-applied timestamps per region.
lee: temporary mitigation: revert to previous config until we have commit-id plumbing? we already see real user quota hits.
maya: I'd prefer not to revert because route-a quota increase is beneficial. Ops: can we throttle config apply frequency until fix is in?
ops-bot: DeployBot: scheduled a hold on automated config rollouts for 2 hours. manual applies allowed with ack.
ali: ok plan sounds good. action items: maya -> router header PR, sameer -> telemetry attribution + metric, katie -> console commit-id card, lee -> apply-window validation in deploy job.
sameer: I'll also add an eval to ensure sample-rate annotated events match routed route in a nightly job.
maya: thanks all. tagging @oncall in case any quota surprises appear. :thumbsup:
lee: thanks — will monitor dashboards and post an update here once we see stable commit id propagation.
